sugestoes.texto: The string "Notes have been hidden by the organizer" is written directly into calEvent.additionalNotes and shown to users in calendar events, but it is not routed through the project's i18n system. The existing TODO even notes this. The PR changed the spelling of this line without resolving the localization gap, so attendees/organizers whose locale is not English still see an untranslated message. Replace the hard-coded string with a translated key (e.g., t("notes_hidden_by_organizer")) and add it to the locale files.

sugestoes.texto: The onError handler concatenates err.data?.code and t(err.message) and shows it in a toast. If the server ever returns a raw error string instead of a translation key, sensitive details (emails, booking IDs, internal error text) could be exposed to the user. Defensively treat err.message as a key only when it is known to be a key, or fall back to a generic translation such as t("unable_to_add_guests") rather than rendering the server message directly.

The uniqueness refine uses `new Set(emails)`, which compares strings case-sensitively. Email addresses are case-insensitive identity data, so `A@example.com` and `a@example.com` pass validation as unique but refer to the same mailbox. Normalize emails with `toLowerCase()` before the Set comparison (and ideally persist the normalized form) to prevent case-variation duplicates and any downstream bypass of case-sensitive attendee or blacklist checks.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
sendAddGuestsEmails never notifies the newly added guests because the formatted event does not contain them, so the newGuests branch is unreachable.
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail reads calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard and throws when the attendee list is empty.
The AddGuests dialog error toast shows the raw server error message and code, which could display internal backend details such as Prisma errors to the user.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout or abort signal. WHY: If the external endpoint hangs, the calling calendar/video request also hangs indefinitely, consuming workers and potentially blocking user-facing operations. HOW: Add an AbortController with a timeout and handle abort errors.

`symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` uses an empty string fallback if the encryption key environment variable is not set. This silently degrades security and could allow decryption/derivation with a known weak key. Fail fast instead (throw or return an error) when the encryption key is missing or shorter than the required 32 bytes.

decodeOAuthState does a bare JSON.parse(req.query.state). A malformed or tampered `state` query param throws SyntaxError, crashing the OAuth callback handler. Use a try/catch and return undefined or a controlled error. The same issue exists in encodeOAuthState.ts.

The guard uses `userId` in a boolean context, so a user id of `0` is treated as absent and the code falls back to the local refresh instead of calling the configured `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Because the parameter is typed `number | null`, the only value that should disable sync is `null` (team credentials). Use an explicit `userId !== null` check so `0` is handled like any other valid user id.

Claims the team-credential branch only checks accepted membership instead of admin rights, letting non-admin members create team credentials.
Claims malformed OAuth state makes JSON.parse throw and crash OAuth callbacks with a 500.
Claims the Office365 video adapter passes the wrong app slug 'msteams' to refreshOAuthTokens.
createOAuthAppCredential only verifies team membership, not admin access, before creating a team credential, so any team member can install OAuth apps for the team via a crafted state.
The app-credential webhook decrypts keys with CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to an empty string when the env var is unset, instead of failing fast.
The app-credential webhook is claimed to accept GET, so a loggable, prefetchable, CSRF-able request carrying the shared secret could overwrite any user's stored OAuth keys.
The app-credential webhook authenticates only by a static shared-secret header, so whoever holds the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials without per-user auth, HMAC or replay protection.
The .env.example tells users to generate CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which is claimed to give only 24 bytes instead of the 32 required by AES256.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the try block, not only for SMS scheduling failures. WHY: Failures from `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, or other unrelated setup can mark a reminder for deletion even though Twilio was never attempted. HOW: Wrap only the `twilio.scheduleSMS` call and the successful update in try/catch, or restructure so retryCount is incremented only when scheduling itself fails.

The catch block logs the raw `error` object from SMS scheduling. Provider error responses often include PII such as recipient/sender phone numbers and message bodies. Redact or summarize the error before logging (e.g., log only the provider error code and a generic message) to prevent leaking sensitive data into application logs.

Claims the failed-send branch does not increment retryCount on the success path.

sugestoes.texto: The assertion `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes even when the switch is not checked because `locator.isChecked()` returns a Promise, and a Promise object is always truthy when passed to the generic `toBeTruthy()` matcher. The PR added a FIXME noting this exact failure mode but left the assertion in place. Replace it with `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`)).toBeChecked()` or `await expect(await page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBe(true)` so the test actually fails when the switch is unchecked.

The disable endpoint locates the supplied backup code with `backupCodes.indexOf(...replaceAll("-", ""))`. This performs a non-constant-time secret comparison and can leak information through response timing. Compare every stored code with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` and only return success/failure after evaluating all candidates.

Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Tests assert equality between flat Prisma.sql template literals and nested Prisma.sql compositions returned by the service. WHY: The service builds compound conditions by interpolating Prisma.Sql fragments into other Prisma.sql templates (e.g., buildFilterConditions and buildOrgAuthorizationCondition), producing Sql objects whose values array contains nested Sql objects; Jest toEqual compares enumerable strings/values properties, so the flat expected literals will not match the nested actual values and the tests will fail. HOW: Assert on the emitted SQL text instead, e.g., expect(conditions.text).toEqual(expected.text), or use a helper that normalizes Prisma.Sql to its flattened text/values before comparison.

`this.filters.eventTypeId` and `this.filters.memberUserId` are optional `number`s, but the code tests them with `if (this.filters.eventTypeId)` and `if (this.filters.memberUserId)`. A caller passing the perfectly valid numeric ID `0` will be treated as if no filter was supplied, causing rows for ID 0 to be excluded or, worse, included when they shouldn't be. Use explicit null/undefined checks such as `this.filters.eventTypeId != null` or `typeof this.filters.eventTypeId !== "undefined"` instead of truthiness.

buildOrgAuthorizationCondition always emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))`. When the organization has no child teams, `teamIds` is empty and PostgreSQL cannot infer the element type of the empty array parameter, causing a runtime error. Guard the team branch the same way the user branch is guarded, and fall back to `1=0` (NOTHING_CONDITION) when both lists are empty.

InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for scope "team", but buildTeamAuthorizationCondition assumes it is defined and interpolates `options.teamId` directly into Prisma.sql. Either keep the schema discriminated-union type in the constructor (requiring teamId for team scope) or validate/throw before using options.teamId, so the previous invariant is not broken.

The exported `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type marks `teamId` as optional, but the `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` and the team-scope authorization logic require it. A caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without `teamId`; runtime validation fails, `this.options` is set to `null`, and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `Prisma.sql`1=0``, producing empty results with no error. Align the public type with the schema so missing `teamId` is caught at compile time, e.g. replace the manual type with `z.input<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>` or use a discriminated union that requires `teamId` for `scope: "team"`.

issues.descricao: Claims org-scope authorization excludes members' personal bookings for organizations without child teams because user ids are fetched only when child teams exist.
Claims removing findMany and returning Prisma.Sql breaks existing callers of InsightsBookingService.
Reports that no failure could be constructed in the changed lines.
Claims toEqual on Prisma.Sql always fails because the service builds nested Sql objects while the test expects a flat literal.

Claims the eventTypeId filter `a OR b` is returned unparenthesized from getFilterConditions, so a caller ANDing it without parentheses would widen results past the filter and authorization conditions.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The script immediately calls comments.appendChild(iframe) without verifying that document.getElementById('discourse-comments') returned an element. WHY: If the host page omits the container or loads the script before the element exists, comments is null and appendChild throws, breaking other scripts on the page. HOW: Guard the appendChild call with an if (comments) check.

WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without verifying the setting is present. WHY: If feed polling is disabled and embed_by_username is blank, the retrieve job raises NoMethodError on nil.downcase instead of failing gracefully. HOW: Return early when the username setting is blank, matching the guard in PollFeed.

WHAT: poll_feed calls open(feed_url).read without a timeout and iterates rss.items without any limit. WHY: A slow or unresponsive feed can hold a worker indefinitely, and a very large feed can consume excessive memory and time importing every item. HOW: Add a read timeout to open and cap the number of items processed per run.

The tests 'does not call perform_retrieve when embeddable_host is not set', 'different than the host of the URL', and 'embed url is not a url' stub SiteSetting.embeddable_host and assert that perform_retrieve is never called. But they also stub retrieve_recently? implicitly only in later tests. The implementation's invalid_host? raises URI::InvalidURIError; if invalid_host? were removed or always returned false, retrieve_recently? would still gate perform_retrieve. Because perform_retrieve is the actual private method being mocked, a bug in invalid_host? does not cause these tests to fail; the tests exercise the mock, not the real host-matching logic. Replace the mock of perform_retrieve with direct assertion about the side effect (e.g. no HTTP fetch, no TopicEmbed import) or call invalid_host? directly and assert its result.

The 'tells the topic retriever to work' and 'creates a topic view' tests stub TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed, TopicRetriever.new, TopicView.new, and the retriever's retrieve method. They therefore pass even if the controller action's real logic for calling TopicRetriever, TopicView, or rendering 'loading' is removed or inverted. These tests assert only that mocks are called with the expected arguments, which by construction matches the test setup; they do not verify the actual response body, template, or that an embed record is created. Add expectations on response.body/rendered_template (e.g. assert the loading partial is rendered when no topic exists and the topic view partial is rendered when one exists) and use real collaborators or at least assert the side effects.

The execute tests stub all three SiteSetting predicates and assert that poll_feed is or is not called. If the execute method's guard condition were changed to ignore any of those settings (e.g. always call poll_feed), the tests using stubs with expects(:poll_feed).never would still catch it, but the 'delegates to poll_feed' test only verifies that poll_feed is called once when all settings are stubbed true; it does not verify that poll_feed actually opens the configured URL, parses it, or calls TopicEmbed.import. The poll_feed method itself has no dedicated test. Add a test that stubs an RSS response and asserts TopicEmbed.import is called with the expected arguments, otherwise a broken parser or wrong argument order could go undetected.

The migration adds cook_method with default: 1, but Post.cook_methods is Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), which maps :regular => 0 and :raw_html => 1. Therefore every existing post and any new post created without an explicit cook_method will be treated as raw_html; Post#cook will return raw instead of cooked HTML, breaking topic rendering across the site. The default should be 0 so the regular cooking pipeline remains the default.

The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`, but `Post.cook_methods` defines `:regular` as 0 and `:raw_html` as 1. This causes all existing posts to default to `raw_html` and skip cooking, returning raw markdown instead of rendered HTML. Change the default to `0` so existing posts keep the regular cooked behavior.

Post.cook_methods maps :regular to 0 and :raw_html to 1, but the migration defaults cook_method to 1. Existing posts will therefore be treated as raw_html and skip the cooking pipeline, rendering raw content instead of cooked HTML.

The if/else block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. ERB emits `end if` verbatim into the generated Ruby source, which is invalid syntax after a multi-line if/else block and will cause the template to raise a syntax error when rendered.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `record_for_host` queries with `lower(host) = ?` but the table has no index on `host`. WHY: This lookup runs on every embedded request, and as the allowed-hosts list grows it degrades to a full table scan. HOW: Add an index on `host` in the migration, ideally `lower(host)` if the database supports expression indexes, or a standard btree index with case-insensitive comparisons in the query.

WHAT: `TopicEmbed.import` now passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)`, which becomes nil when no embeddable host matches the URL. WHY: Previously the default `SiteSetting.embed_category` was always used; feed polling and import scripts that call `import` directly can now create topics with no explicit category, changing behavior for URLs that do not match a configured host. HOW: Fall back to the uncategorized category or the old default when `eh` is blank, matching the controller's blank-category handling.

`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` treats `0` and empty string the same as `nil`. If category id `0` is ever meaningful, it will be silently replaced. Use `if host.category_id.nil?` to test for an explicitly absent value rather than any falsy/blank value.

The describe block is named 'allows_embeddable_host' but the model method added in this PR is 'host_allowed?'. The test description names a non-existent method, which is confusing and will break navigation/expectations. Rename the describe block to 'host_allowed?' to match the actual API.

The input placeholder is hardcoded English text 'example.com' instead of using the I18n translation mechanism. This bypasses localization and will appear untranslated for non-English users. Add a translation key (e.g. admin.embedding.host_placeholder) and use it here.

The spec added for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only checks that it is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. It does not exercise create, update, or destroy. Those actions could be completely broken and this spec would still pass, so it does not verify the controller behaviour it appears to cover. Add request specs for the actual actions, or at least assert that saving/destroying a host has the expected side effects.

The spec added for Admin::EmbeddingController only checks that it inherits from Admin::AdminController. It does not call show or update, which in this PR return a serialized embedding object. Those actions could be removed or broken and the spec would still pass. Add tests that hit the routes and verify the serialized response contains the embeddable hosts.

sugestoes.texto: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` asks ImageMagick to read from and write to the same file. The model's `convert_with` builds a `convert <from> ... <to>` shell command and assumes distinct paths; overwriting the source during conversion can corrupt or truncate the upload. Downsize to a temporary path and then replace the original.

sugestoes.texto: The add_members and remove_member actions read params.require(:group_id), but the routes declared in config/routes.rb are member routes under `resources :groups`, so Rails supplies the group id as `params[:id]`. This mismatch will cause ParameterMissing on every add/remove request. Change `params.require(:group_id)` to `params.require(:id)` (or declare the routes with `param: :group_id`).

params[:alias_level].present? returns false for the integer 0, so selecting the "nobody" alias level (value 0) leaves the existing alias_level unchanged. Use an existence check that accepts 0 while still skipping absent/blank values.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves the underlying hash empty, so every method other than `[]` (e.g. `each`, `keys`, `defaults`, `map`) sees an empty collection. WHY: This violates the I18n::Locale::Fallbacks/Hash contract; any future caller that iterates or inspects `I18n.fallbacks` will get no locales even though `I18n.fallbacks[:en]` returns a fallback chain. HOW: Delegate storage to a real Hash by calling `super` in `[]` and populating defaults explicitly, or do not inherit from Hash and instead implement only the small interface I18n::Backend::Fallbacks actually needs (e.g. `def [](locale); ... end`).

sugestoes.texto: updateDevice updates only rows WHERE updated_at BETWEEN device.UpdatedAt - 30d AND device.UpdatedAt + 1m. If the existing row's updated_at is older than 30 days, the UPDATE matches no rows and CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The caller in client.go then fails anonymous authentication. The limit-reached path should still allow an existing device to be renewed/updated regardless of age (or fall back to an insert when the device_id already exists), rather than rejecting the request.

The error message 'device limit reached' is user-facing but is a hard-coded English literal. It bypasses Grafana's i18n/translation system, so users in other locales will see untranslated English text. This string should be passed through the project's translation mechanism (e.g., i18n.Translate) and added to the relevant locale file(s).

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware returns a middleware closure that reuses the same *MetricsMiddleware instance and mutates its `next` field. WHY: Decorating more than one client with the returned middleware overwrites the chain and, because the metrics are already registered on the same registerer, a second factory use can panic with duplicate metric registration. HOW: Inside the closure create a new *MetricsMiddleware (or a shallow copy of the registered metrics struct) with its own `next` pointer, registering the metrics only once at factory construction time.

WHAT: QueryData and CallResource look up the plugin target from the registry twice per request (once for size and once for duration). WHY: The duplicated registry lookup doubles the work on every plugin request for the two instrumented endpoints. HOW: Resolve the target once per method and pass it into both instrumentPluginRequestSize and instrumentPluginRequest, or add a helper that records size and duration with a single lookup.
The doc comment for `pluginRequestSize` says 'returned' which appears inaccurate (it tracks outgoing request sizes), but this is in internal metric help text.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Every Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection spawns a new goroutine that can live up to 10 seconds with no concurrency limit or backpressure. WHY: Under high write throughput this creates unbounded goroutine fanout and memory growth, especially if the legacy store is slow or times out. HOW: Bound concurrency with a worker pool or semaphore, or use a rate-limited background queue for legacy writes.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The HTML tag detector and anchor matcher use case-sensitive regular expressions (`<[a-z]+[^>]*>` and `]*>`) even though HTML element names are case-insensitive. WHY: The OWASP sanitizer canonicalizes tag names to lowercase, so a translation with `text` or `` is not matched by the anchor pre-check and is then normalized by the sanitizer to lowercase, making `sanitized != value` and causing a false-positive "Illegal HTML" build failure. HOW: Compile `HTML_TAGS` and `ANCHOR_PATTERN` with `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (or add `A-Z` to the character classes for tags and `A` for anchors) so the verifier treats HTML case-insensitively.

New error/reporting paths in verifySafeHtml() include java.io.File instances (file/englishFile) whose toString() yields absolute paths, so build logs will contain absolute filesystem paths. This occurs at lines 70 and 79 (RuntimeException with file/englishFile) and line 111 (messages.add with file). This is minor information disclosure, but it is already present in unchanged code at line 53 (MojoExecutionException with file) and is standard output for Maven plugins; the PR does not introduce a new class of sensitive-data exposure. No data-exposure defect of the assigned class is present. Note: line 157 (messages.add with matcher.group()) echoes anchor tags, which is expected behavior for a verifier and does not constitute disclosure of sensitive data.

Replace the FileInputStream-based PropertyResourceBundle construction with UTF-8 Reader-based construction. The existing verify() path uses Files.readString (UTF-8), but PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) decodes as ISO-8859-1, so the HTML verifier interprets the same file differently than the duplicate-key verifier. This corrupts UTF-8 translations (e.g., the modified Chinese properties files) and can produce incorrect 'Illegal HTML' results or garbled error messages. Use Files.newBufferedReader(file.toPath(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8) for both bundle reads.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` and `hasPermission(String)` do not verify that returned `Permission.resourceId` matches the resource being evaluated. WHY: If `root.evaluatePermission` returns permissions for other resources (e.g. a different client or the all-clients resource), the loops will grant access based solely on matching scopes, allowing a permission meant for one client to satisfy a check for another. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission filters on `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`, so the same defensive check should be applied here. HOW: Add the resourceId equality guard inside the permission loops in `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, `hasPermission(String)`, and `hasGrantedPermission`.

WHAT: `getClientsWithPermission(String)` loads every client resource of type Clients and evaluates permissions for each one. WHY: For realms with many clients this produces O(N) authorization evaluations on every caller such as `AvailableRoleMappingResource`, causing linear slowdown of role-mapping and client-listing operations. HOW: Consider evaluating a single all-clients resource first and returning early when a global grant exists; otherwise keep per-client evaluation but bound it with pagination or cache granted scopes per request.

The Javadoc says 'Or if the caller has a permission to {@link AdminPermissionManagement#VIEW_SCOPE} the client. For V2 only: Also if the caller has a permission to {@link org.keycloak.authorization.AdminPermissionsSchema#VIEW} all clients.' However, ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) only checks canView()/canConfigure(client) and AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW; it never evaluates AdminPermissionManagement.VIEW_SCOPE. The 'Also' wording is misleading because the V1 per-client check is absent in V2.

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides isPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel) and setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, even though these methods are part of the ClientPermissionEvaluator interface contract. Since MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, callers holding a ClientPermissionEvaluator reference that invoke these methods will break. Either provide a V2 implementation that honors the interface contract, add default no-op behavior to the interface, or update all consumers to avoid calling these methods on V2.

The tests call getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) and .get(0) without checking that the list contains enough elements. If the realm has fewer default scopes than assumed, the test throws IndexOutOfBoundsException before it can verify the intended ForbiddenException behavior. Guard the index access with an isEmpty()/size() check or select a scope safely, and fail with a clear message if none are available.

The ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false), but in the V2 permission path clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, deleting a client will therefore raise an unhandled exception and abort the transaction. The cleanup should either be skipped for V2, or ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled should be a no-op (or properly clean up V2 authorization resources).

In V2 there is no per-client permission toggle, but the client-removal cleanup path in AdminPermissions.java still invokes setPermissionsEnabled(...). Make this method a no-op instead of throwing UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client does not fail when admin fine-grained authz V2 is enabled.

For multi-host events this can map an override to the wrong UTC day. Use `date.timeZone` (falling back to `organizerTimeZone` only when absent) inside the `dateOverrides.find` callback when formatting/comparing `date.start` and `date.end`, and update the `dateOverrides` parameter type to include `timeZone?: string`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The denial cache stores negative authorization decisions for `shortCacheTTL` (30 seconds) and is never invalidated. WHY: If a user is denied access, then an admin grants permission to that exact resource, subsequent Check calls hit the cached denial and return false until the TTL expires, contradicting the PR goal of letting users access newly authorized dashboards and folders. HOW: Invalidate the matching denial cache entry whenever the user's permissions for the action are refreshed or updated; alternatively, skip denial caching for wildcard-capable actions or reduce the TTL if invalidation is not feasible.

WHAT: When permissions are found in the permission cache but `checkPermission` returns false, the code increments `permissionCacheUsage` with label `false` as if the cache missed. WHY: This metric conflates actual cache misses with cache hits that did not grant access, making cache-hit observability inaccurate. HOW: Increment the cache-usage metric with `true` immediately after a successful `getCachedIdentityPermissions` return, before evaluating whether the permission grants access.

Check consults permDenialCache before the permission cache and DB, and only writes to it when the DB lookup denies. If a user's permissions change from deny to allow, the stale denial entry remains for the cache TTL and continues to deny access even though the current permission set would grant it. Either delete the denial entry when a Check finally allows, or avoid negative caching in the authorization path.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags (e.g., 0x22) because it only masks the low 5 bits of the tag byte. WHY: DER/BER requires INTEGER to be primitive; accepting constructed encodings silently parses malformed input as a valid integer, diverging from BouncyCastle's strict parser. HOW: Reject the constructed bit by checking `(tag & ASN1Encoder.CONSTRUCTED) == 0` before reading the value.

WHAT: The ignored-providers log calls `logger.debugf(builder.toString())`, but debugf expects a format string. WHY: A provider class name containing `%` (e.g., from a shaded/proxied jar) would cause `MissingFormatArgumentException` and abort detection; even without that, it is the wrong logging API. HOW: Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` and avoid the trailing comma.

When qLength < bytes.length, the method copies only the lowest qLength bytes. For a malformed or non-minimal DER integer whose value exceeds the curve coordinate size, this silently changes the numeric value instead of rejecting the signature. It should throw if bytes.length > qLength + 1 (after allowing at most one sign-padding zero) or if stripping that zero still leaves more than qLength bytes.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking isPresent(), so a missing recovery-codes credential in both federated and local storage throws NoSuchElementException. WHY: This crashes the login form rendering when the credential is absent, instead of failing gracefully or redirecting to setup. HOW: Check credentialModelOpt.isPresent() before .get(), and throw a meaningful runtime exception or redirect if the credential is missing.

WHAT: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the raw generated recovery codes to JSON and passes them as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel to user storage, while the local-storage path stores hashed codes through RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider. WHY: A user storage provider that persists the CredentialInput value (as the test BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does) stores recovery codes in plain text, exposing high-value backup credentials if the external store or its backups are compromised. HOW: Pass the codes in a form that lets the storage provider hash them before persistence, or document that user storage providers must hash the value themselves and update the test provider to hash before storing and compare hashed values during validation.

The recovery code verification uses direct String.equals() on hashed secrets, which is vulnerable to timing attacks. Use a constant-time comparison function (e.g., MessageDigest.isEqual) to compare the hashed input against each stored hashed recovery code.

The recovery key validation compares raw input recovery codes against stored values using key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()) inside a stream, which performs a non-constant-time comparison and leaks timing information. Use a constant-time comparison function for each candidate recovery code.

createRecoveryCodesCredential passes the raw generatedCodes JSON to user storage via updateCredential, while falling back to the credentialModel (which holds hashed codes) for local storage. This creates a representation split: user-storage providers receive and typically store plaintext recovery codes, whereas the local DB provider stores hashed codes. The validation path in the test user storage then compares raw input to raw stored codes, inconsistent with the normal hashed validation. The method should pass equivalent credential material to both paths, e.g., by using the credential model's serialized/hashed data for user storage as well, or by documenting and enforcing that user-storage providers must hash the received codes.

Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.

sugestoes.texto: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged, while BasePaginator.value_from_cursor returns cursor.value + 1 for prev cursors. Since build_queryset uses this value as the pagination boundary, backward navigation will use an inclusive instead of exclusive boundary and can return the cursor row again or skip rows. Restore the prev-cursor increment or call the base implementation to keep boundary semantics consistent.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls getattr(item, self.key) directly and omits the callable-key branch that BasePaginator.get_item_key provides. This contradicts the docstring's claim of backward compatibility and will raise TypeError for any queryset ordered by a callable key. Add the same isinstance(self.key, Callable) branch used by BasePaginator.

sugestoes.texto: The truthiness check `if client_sample_rate:` treats a legitimate `0.0` sample rate as missing and silently skips setting `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`. A client sample rate of `0.0` is a valid boundary value meaning "sample nothing / record everything at the client", so it should be propagated explicitly. Replace the truthiness check with an explicit `is not None` (and ideally also validate it is a number, not e.g. an empty string) before converting to float.

The comments on lines 3626-3627 say 'First bucket has 1 event' and 'Second bucket has 1 event', but the assertions on the same lines check that the count equals 10. The count is 10 because the single stored event has client_sample_rate=0.1 and upsampling multiplies by 1/0.1. The comments describe the raw stored events, while the assertions check the upsampled metric value, so the comments disagree with the code they annotate. Update the comments to explain that the bucket contains 1 event that is upsampled to a count of 10, or remove the stale comment.

`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `True` for the `errors` dataset, so `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. The visible diff only adds the `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`; if the errors dataset config does not inherit it, an errors-dataset `count()` query on allowlisted projects will fail with an unknown function error. Either add the function to the errors dataset config or restrict the rewrite to datasets where the function is known to exist.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets() iterates range(start, max_offset + 1) to find the highest contiguous completed offset. WHY: If offsets are sparse (log-compacted topic, skipped filtered messages), the loop runs in O(offset gap) rather than O(backlog), which can become very large and stalls the commit thread. HOW: Sort the tracked offsets and walk the sorted list to find the highest contiguous completed offset, which is O(n log n) in the number of tracked offsets.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `process_batch` reads `val['end_timestamp_precise']` from a raw `ingest_spans_v1.SpanEvent`, but that Kafka schema only guarantees `end_timestamp`. WHY: Every real span message will raise `KeyError`, crashing the consumer batch. HOW: Construct `Span` using the actual schema field `val['end_timestamp']` (converted to the precise float representation the buffer expects).

No validation that end_timestamp_precise is finite before using it as a Redis ZADD score; Redis rejects NaN, though the schema (sentry_kafka_schemas.schema_types.ingest_spans_v1.SpanEvent) and rapidjson are assumed to guarantee a valid number.

`set_key` was accurate when this key held a Redis Set, but the PR now writes it with `zadd` and reads it with `zscan`. The identifier implies plain set semantics while the implementation depends on sorted-set behavior (ordering, zpopmin trimming). Rename it to `zset_key` or `segment_key` so the code contract matches the Redis data type.

test_backpressure constructs all spans with the same end_timestamp_precise, so it cannot catch a regression where the buffer ignores or misuses the timestamp score. Use distinct timestamps and assert that the sorted-set ordering and eviction logic are honored when backpressure limits are applied.

issues.descricao: Claims the redirect-resolution limit was silently cut from 10000 to 1000, so segment trees deeper than 1000 are no longer joined, and the comment still mentions 10k.
Claims a non-root span whose key equals the resolved set key unions the key with itself and then unlinks it, deleting the buffered segment.
Claims a span message missing end_timestamp_precise raises KeyError and aborts the whole batch.
Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch passes cursor.offset directly into queryset slicing when advanced features are enabled.

Claims OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies floor/ceil to a datetime key, raising TypeError.
Claims accessing organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError when organization_context is None.
process_batch indexes end_timestamp_precise directly, so a span without the field raises KeyError and fails the whole consumer batch.
Claims span_count counts pre-existing spans in set_key, so zpopmin evicts far more than the overflow above 1000 and discards valid spans.
SDK-supplied end_timestamp_precise is used as the ZSET eviction score, so an attacker sending far-future timestamps could keep their spans and force eviction of legitimate ones.
Each span insert runs up to two ZUNIONSTORE copies of the segment set plus ZCARD/ZPOPMIN, making segment building O(N^2) on the ingest hot path.
